claims.text: Ab initio calculations using VASP can predict the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy oxides.
The relevant high-entropy oxides can have varying compositions.
Composition can be varied when investigating magnetic behavior in high-entropy oxides.
Magnetic behavior in high-entropy oxides can be investigated over variable temperatures.
Magnetic behavior in high-entropy oxides can be investigated under variable magnetic fields.
Configurational entropy is associated with the magnetic and electrical properties of high-entropy oxides.
The average ionic radius of A-site cations influences magnetic properties in high-entropy oxide perovskites.
The correlation between electrical and magnetic properties is caused by configurational entropy.
The correlation between electrical and magnetic properties is caused by the average ionic radius of A-site cations.
Configurational entropy and A-site ionic radius influence indirect super-exchange interactions.
Configurational entropy and A-site ionic radius promote the formation of ferromagnetic nanoclusters.
Specific high-entropy-oxide compositions and processing routes produce ferromagnetic ground states.
Paramagnetic or antiferromagnetic behavior provides a baseline relative to ferromagnetic high-entropy oxides.
There are compositional boundaries beyond which ferromagnetic ground states are not observed.
There are processing boundaries beyond which ferromagnetic ground states are not observed.
Prediction of ferromagnetic ground states is uncertain because high-entropy-oxide systems are complex and ab initio calculations have limitations.
SQUID magnetometry and neutron diffraction can be used to investigate magnetic properties and magnetic ordering in high-entropy oxides.
Failure to observe a ferromagnetic ground state in a composition and processing route predicted to have one would falsify the stated prediction.
